All Campus 2 PCs (PC1-4, dc_pc5) report they cannot reach
Campus 1 or the WAN. They CAN still ping their own gateways
(10.5.0.254, 10.6.0.254) on sshswitch. Find what cut Campus 2's
uplink.

injection.action: bring down the bond toward router17 (eth6+eth7)

post_inject_check.command: ip link show bond0 | grep -c "state DOWN"

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: sshswitch bond0 (LACP to router17)
Mechanism: bond0 is sshswitch's only L3 uplink toward router17,
  carrying tagged VLAN 100 (servers — excluded from hosts),
  VLAN 200, and untagged VLAN 1 traffic toward the OSPF
  backbone. With bond0 down, sshswitch loses OSPF adjacency
  with router17 and Campus 2 becomes an island. Local gateways
  still respond because they're SVIs on sshswitch itself.
Localization: sshswitch
Root cause: bond0 (port-channel toward router17) is down on sshswitch
Fix: `ip link set bond0 up` on sshswitch
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set bond0 up` on sshswitch

line.command: ip link show bond0 | grep -c "state DOWN"

agent.diagnosis_text:
The Campus 2 uplink is broken because sshswitch's `bond0` interface has been administratively shut down. sshswitch acts as the Layer-3 gateway for VLANs 5 and 6 (10.5.0.254/24 and 10.6.0.254/24) and uses a bonded interface (bond0, comprising eth6 and eth7 — the two physical links to router17) to carry inter-campus and WAN traffic over the 55.5.1.0/24 subnet. Both physical slave interfaces (eth6, eth7) are physically up and their bonding-driver MII status reports "up", but `ip link show bond0` shows `state DOWN` with no `LOWER_UP` flag, indicating the bond was brought down administratively (i.e., `ip link set bond0 down` was executed).

With bond0 down, bridge br_v1 (which holds the 55.5.1.2/24 uplink IP) has only eth0 (the switch4 access side) as an active member. OSPF Hello packets that sshswitch sends out on 55.5.1.0/24 go toward switch4 and never reach router17. Simultaneously, OSPF Hellos arriving from router17 on eth6/eth7 are discarded because bond0 is down. The result is that sshswitch forms zero OSPF adjacencies (confirmed: empty neighbor table), receives no OSPF routes, and therefore has no default route or any route to Campus 1 / WAN subnets. Traffic from Campus 2 PCs arrives at sshswitch and is silently dropped. Router17 also never learns the 10.5.0.0/24 or 10.6.0.0/24 prefixes via OSPF, so return traffic would equally fail.

Corrective fix: On sshswitch, run `ip link set bond0 up`. This restores the bond0 logical interface, allows OSPF adjacency to form with router17 over 55.5.1.0/24, and propagates all routes in both directions, restoring full Campus 2 reachability.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies sshswitch as the affected device and attributes the bond0/OSPF failure to it.
The report explicitly identifies bond0 as the administratively down port-channel uplink (eth6+eth7) to router17.
The writeup never states that the switch's local SVIs still respond (it instead says traffic is silently dropped), so it fails to distinguish that local gateway SVIs remain up.
Correctly instructs to bring bond0 up on sshswitch (ip link set bond0 up), matching the expected fix.

The agent's logs contain direct observations (bond0 down on sshswitch, physical slaves up, ping to router17 failing, router17 bond0 up, empty OSPF neighbor table on sshswitch) that support the stated conclusion; the inference that admin-down bond0 broke OSPF and caused isolation follows logically and the essential alternatives were checked.
